newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares rise 2.3 pct on govt hopes, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares rise 2.3 pct on govt hopes, off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose sharply on Thursday amid new government prospects to end months-long political uncertainty after the resignation of the Islamist-led coalition late on Wednesday, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed up 36 points, or 2.3 percent at 1,601, but fell from an afternoon high of 1,620 on profit-taking. Trade volume leapt to 17.83 trillion lira ($122.2 million) from Wednesday's 13.86 trillion ($95.3 million).

"The market looked good today. Buying based on expectations of new government alternatives may continue until a new coalition is established," said Kerim Sarc from Abn Amro Hoare Govett securities, Istanbul.

President Suleyman Demirel kicked off a difficult bid to find a new government by meeting opposition leaders after Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned following a months-long dispute with the secularist army over rising Islamist activism.
